comparison.phase1_seismology: R^2=0.9927 over 3 decades, slope clearly nonzero
comparison.phase2_sp500_this_test: 8.4 sigma (Wald) / 8.4 sigma (t-test) / 5.1 sigma (bootstrap). Lower than Phase 3 because n_main=318 and only 30 lag-bins, but still well above 5-sigma null rejection. The qualitative Omori-decay claim stands; the headline R^2=0.71 is lower than Phase 1's 0.9927 because the daily-band has only ~1.5 decades of dynamic range vs Phase 1's 3 decades.

verdict: Slope-zero null rejected at >8 sigma (all three tests agree). The Phase 2 Omori p=0.286 is statistically distinguishable from the flat-rate null. Lower-than-Phase-1 R^2 reflects a narrower lag-band dynamic range, not a marginal-significance fit.
